header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Unanimously Accept Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) as Khalifah

blocks.text:
had gathered with Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) in the orchard of the Banu Saa'idah where they intended taking the pledge of allegiance. Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) stood up in alarm and hastened towards the Ansaar fearing that they may introduce something strange into Islaam. En route they happened to meet two truthful men; Hadhrat Uwaym bin Saa'idah (RA) and Hadhrat Ma'n bin Adi (RA). When the two men asked where the others were off to, the others replied, "We are off to see your people (the Ansaar) concerning what we have heard about their activities." The two men said, "You may return because you can never be opposed and nothing can be done without your approval." Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "We refused to listen to them and continued. In the meantime, I was preparing a speech to say to them. When we eventually reached them, we found them all around Sa'd bin Ubaadah who was lying on a bed due to illness."
When the Muhaajireen arrived, the Ansaar addressed them saying, "O assembly of the Quraysh! Let there be an Ameer from amongst us and another from amongst you." Hadhrat Hubaab bin Mundhir (RA) added, "I have the perfect solution and the best medicine for this. By Allaah! If you agree, we could make this as pleasant as a young camel." "Take it easy," said Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). As he started talking, he first bade Hadhrat Umar (RA) to be silent. Thereafter, he praised Allaah and said, "O assembly of Ansaar! I swear by Allaah that we do not deny your virtues. We neither deny the high status that you have reached in Islaam nor the rights that we owe you. However, even you acknowledge that no other tribe enjoys the status that the Quraysh enjoys amongst all the Arabs. You also know well that the Arabs will unite only under the leadership of one of them. While we (from the Quraysh) shall be the leaders, you (Ansaar) shall be our ministers. Fear Allaah! Do not cause divisions in Islaam and do not be the first to introduce something strange into Islaam. I have selected two men (referring to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA)). Whichever of them you choose to pledge your allegiance, you may be rest assured that he is dependable."
Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "By Allaah! There was nothing that I wanted said which Abu Bakr (RA) did not say except this part (where he named me as a potential candidate). I swear by Allaah that I would prefer being killed, then brought back to life and then being killed again for no crime on my part rather than being appointed leader of a community that includes Abu Bakr (RA)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then addressed the gathering saying, "O assembly of Ansaar! O assembly of Muslims! Indeed the person most worthy of leadership after Rasulullaah ﷺ is 'the second of the two when they were in the cave'. He is Abu Bakr (RA) who was clearly the very first (to enter Islaam)."
Hadhrat Umar (RA) then grabbed the hand of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) but before he could pledge his allegiance to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), an Ansaari beat him to it. All the other people followed suit and no attention was given to Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA). [^1]
Ibn Abi Shayba, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.139).
